I’m genuinely upset with the experience I had at Dosa Dosa.

We travelled quite far just to visit this outlet. Before heading out, we double-checked the timings on Google, which clearly showed that the restaurant was open from 6:30 AM to 11:00 pm. However, when we arrived, we were simply told that it was closed.

There was no sign or notice displayed outside indicating the closure, and Google still showed it as open. To make matters worse, we could see a few people inside and it looked like some sort of shoot was taking place. If that was the situation, the management should have at least updated their timings online or put up a proper notice outside.

The response we received was a very casual “Sorry, we’re closed,” and the staff immediately went back to what they were doing. There was no explanation, no apology beyond that, and no effort to assist us in any way.

When customers make the effort to travel specifically to your outlet, basic communication and courtesy should be a priority. Overall, very poor coordination and disappointing customer service.

featured_reviews.review_text:
**“Extremely disappointing and mentally frustrating experience. I ordered 2 Masala Dosa and 2 boxes of Medu Wada (each box containing 4 pieces, around ₹211 each), along with a watermelon juice add-on.

Shockingly, I did not receive the Medu Wada at all. I only received 2 boxes containing Masala Dosa with chutney and sambhar.

When I contacted the restaurant, they first told me to check properly and said there should be 3 boxes. After confirming with their kitchen, they firmly stated that everything was packed and sent correctly. Then they shifted the responsibility, saying if anything happens during transit, it is Zomato and the delivery partner’s issue.

But this is where the real problem lies. Instead of taking accountability or properly investigating, responsibility is being passed around. This creates a system where no one is answerable, and the only person who suffers is the customer who paid honestly.

Also, blaming the delivery stage so casually makes no sense. A delivery partner is not just a middle person—they are the backbone of this entire system. Without them, restaurants cannot deliver food and platforms cannot function. Indirectly shifting blame without clarity or resolution only reflects poor coordination and lack of accountability in the entire process.

In the end, both the restaurant and Zomato get paid, but the customer is left with incomplete food, no proper explanation, no immediate support, and only different excuses from everyone involved.

This is not just about a missing item, it reflects a deeper issue of responsibility, coordination, and customer respect. Very irresponsible service and a truly disappointing experience.”**

“If the system cannot ensure accountability, then the customer will always be the weakest and most ignored part of it.”

featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshinayan in Juhu is a highly recommended, budget-friendly spot for anyone seeking authentic South Indian cuisine in Mumbai. Despite its simple decor, it remains a favorite among locals and celebrities for its consistently delicious food and quick hospitality.

Ambiance and Service
The restaurant features a peaceful, straightforward dining environment where staff serve guests in traditional South Indian attire. Because of its immense popularity, visitors should anticipate a wait time of 30 to 45 minutes, especially during weekends. Fortunately, once you are seated, the kitchen operates with remarkable efficiency and brings out orders within minutes.

Food and Specialties
The menu focuses heavily on perfectly executed classic staples that are incredibly flavourful and reasonably priced. Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. Large groups can enjoy a massive 4-foot long family dosa, and every visit should conclude with a hot cup of their signature filter coffee.

featured_reviews.review_text:

The seating is spread out , the space is nice and bright and very clean . The aircon facing us was on high cool so we had them turn it down and they obliged .
The food was amazing - for drinks we had the fresh sugar cane juice ,filter coffee and fresh lime soda , all of which were really good - the coffee could have been hotter .
Starters we had rasam vada & kancheepuram idli to share - both were well made - vada was soft and so was the idli. The rasam was top notch.
Mains we shared a ghee masala dosa , masala vada and pesarattu -all three were really good .
Desserts we had were falooda kulfi, kesar pista kulfi and filter coffee affogato. All three did not disappoint.
Service would have been 5* except for a very reluctant server who stood across the table staring at everything but did not take orders or help.
The restaurant sells two kinds of podi and rasam/ sambar powder in their own brand .

The starters were packed with authentic flavours, the main course was rich and comforting, and the desserts were the perfect sweet ending. Truly, some of the best Kerala cuisine I’ve ever tasted.
What makes this place even more special is the ambience—it genuinely transports you to Kerala. Serene, beautiful, and thoughtfully designed, it creates a calming escape right in the middle of Juhu.
The staff deserves a special mention—warm, attentive, and incredibly kind, they make you feel right at home. It’s also wonderfully kid-friendly, making it perfect for family outings.
This is not just a one-time visit kind of place—I’ll definitely be coming back with family and friends. If you love great food, great vibes, and heartfelt hospitality, this one is an absolute must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Umesh Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:

Over all it’s an excellent place and would love to visit this place again

The kanava crispy fry was a let down, it's just fried squid with no flavour.  They didn't give us any dips or chutney with it.
Chemmeen manga curry was the hero of the afternoon. Tasty, tangy, full of prawns and raw mango. What's not to like. We paired them with freshly made appams and neer dosa.

South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

While our experience, the food, and the service were great, what surprised me was a South Indian restaurant whose Sambar was so average. That being said, multiple visits to The Tanjore Tiffin Room are in my future.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Nicely presented menus, friendly staff, delicious home style recipes served in chunky brass dishes, complementary colours and textures.

Small tasting bowls of curry and rice samples are a prelude to the main course. The food is heavy, so go easy on the ordering!

We had hardly finished our starters, when the main courses piled up on the table...service could be staggered slightly.

Loos are off a small landing and could be cleaner. On our way out, the entrance area had become jammed with waiting guests, a tight situation, as were the takeaway boxes, which were over-stuffed.

featured_reviews.name: Daniel Harrington
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely stunning in every way.

Fell across this place via Google maps and waited until 10pm for a table (our fault we didn't book), however it did not disappoint.

Genuinely a top 5 all time restaurant for me. The food, the service, the ambience absolutely top tier. I have never had Indian food (from any region) as flavourful. The staff explained the concept and dishes incredibly well and the taster platter to help decide what to order was so fantastic. I would recommend this to absolutely everyone who lives in or is visiting Mumbai.

Thanks for an unforgettable night.

Please open up in London!!

featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.

featured_reviews.name: Sukanya T

featured_reviews.name: Anil Mahato

Please do visit and try once, highly recommended for taste, value for money and authentic foods.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a new South Indian food spot in the city so I had to check it out. Nanna House in Bandra is serving Andhra style food and I tried their specials. The Karam Podi Dosa is your usual slick dosa, but with Karam Podi masala which was too spicy for me. The Pesarattu, a healthy moong dal dosa, was perfect though. I really enjoyed it. Another of their healthy offerings is the Millet Cone Idli, served in this very cute manner. It is plain and pasty, and a must try. All of this comes with 4 chutneys, each with their own kick. What you can’t miss here at all is their Filter Kaapi Soft Serve - it’s like creamy cold coffee. So good. Overall, this place offers unique and healthy options, so if that’s what you like, check it out.

featured_reviews.name: sucheta thakur
featured_reviews.review_text:
If there’s one place Bandra needs to start forming lines for, it’s @nannahouseindia on 16th Road. This Andhra-style spot is all set to change the way Bandra — actually, Bombay — experiences South Indian food. And yes, maybe it sounds like I’m exaggerating… but one meal here is enough to prove why I’m not.

From the moment the food arrived, everything reminded me of the kind of flavours that feel simple, comforting, yet absolutely unforgettable.

We started with the Pesarattu, beautifully stuffed with upma — a combination that instantly transported me back to Hyderabad. The texture, the seasoning, the warmth… it just hits in the most nostalgic way.

Next up was the star of the show: the Butter Masala Dosa. Cooked in Amul butter and finished with a generous dollop of white butter, this dosa is easily one of the best in Bombay. Crisp edges, a soft centre, flavour-packed masala — truly dosa heaven.

The Butter Podi Idli followed the same theme — soft idlis coated in podi and topped with white butter. Comforting, buttery, and delicious in every bite.

And of course, no South Indian meal is complete without Filter Coffee. Their version is strong, aromatic, and balanced — exactly how a proper filter coffee should be.

But the surprise winner? The Filter Coffee Soft Serve. Smooth, perfectly sweet, full of coffee flavour — honestly, the perfect end to this meal. I’d go back just for this. ❤️

In a city overflowing with restaurants, Nanna House India stands out for its authenticity, warmth, and flavour-packed dishes. What are you waiting for? This is the place Bandra needs queues for — and trust me, once you try it, you’ll understand why.

featured_reviews.name: Vardhita Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overall, the experience was okay, but they definitely need to work on their management. It was quite crowded, and the person handling it wasn’t able to manage things well. Plus, the kiosk machine for ordering and payment wasn’t working, which made it a bit inconvenient.
Food Feedback:
1) Karam Podi Dosa – Felt dry and was served cold.
2) Ghee Podi Idli – Hardly any podi, and the idli was way too soft — almost like it wasn’t cooked properly.
3) Millet Cone Idli – Nice and different, but they can totally skip the ice-cream stick.
4) Filter Kaapi – Tasted good, but sugar should be on the table. We had to ask twice before we got it.
5) Chutney – Would be great if they could increase the quantity a bit.

featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am so in love with Andhra cuisine — those soft, soft idlis and dosas are my absolute weakness! I recently visited a new place that opened in Bandra, and it’s perfect for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
The food here is pure bliss. The chutney, the sambhar — the authenticity is just amazing. The millet cone idli was my favourite!
We also tried their Ghee Podi Idli and Button Vada — so fresh and so yummy, I just couldn’t say no.
The Karam Masala Dosa was nice and crispy, and the Poori Saagu was absolutely ultimate.
Overall, the food is superb and I truly enjoyed every bit of it.
And lastly… Filter Coffee is a must before you wrap up your meal.
Do check this place out if you’re an idli fan just like me!
They have limited menu but super tasty 🤤

featured_reviews.name: Farhan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you are searching for authentic Andhra food in Bandra, Nanna House is a place you should not miss. This South Indian cafe specialises in traditional Andhra cuisine, and the flavours truly reflect home-style cooking. The millet cone idlis were soft and wholesome, and the podi idlis had the perfect balance of ghee and spice.

The dosa selection is excellent. The karam podi dosa was spicy, crisp, and full of flavour, while the butter masala dosa was comforting and indulgent. Every dish felt freshly prepared and true to South Indian food traditions, making it one of the better South Indian restaurants in Bandra.

The highlight for me was the putharekulu dessert, a rare Andhra sweet that is difficult to find in Mumbai. Light, ghee-rich, and delicately sweet, it ended the meal beautifully. Add a cup of traditional filter coffee and the experience feels complete. Highly recommended for anyone looking for the best Andhra restaurant in Bandra.

featured_reviews.name: Mommy OnDuty
featured_reviews.review_text: Nice cozy ambience with awesome south indian food. All dishes tastes delicious and is priced appropriate for the pocket. Dont forget to try its Karam podi dosa, andhra style poori sagu, ghee dosa with authentic filter coffee….

featured_reviews.name: 1TeaspoonLove
featured_reviews.review_text:
Nanna house is an Andhra style kitchen serving authentic Andhra food.

The dishes are served with 4 types of chutneys and sambar.

The idlis were super soft almost melted in the mouth. We loved the Babai idli which were dipped in ghee topped with white butter. So good! The podi idli was good too.

We tried the Karam podi and pesarattu .. both were crisp and tasted good. The karam podi was garlicky and spicy.

The filter coffee was good but the filter coffee soft serve was excellent. Must try. It was smooth creamy and perfect.

Overall good food.

Very neat and tidy but clean place, with only four tables on the ground floor and probably another four on the first floor. Very simple interior and ambience that makes us feel at ease.

Very good service by a very efficient person Tiwari ji who is always on the move and taking care of every person on every table, without a need to call again and remind for anything. A very humble person with smiling face, Tiwari ji caters to all our requests with full energy throughout. He is Occasionally assisted or supported by the owner of the place who supervises all activities, in the kitchen and with the guests alike.

Now, coming to the food part, a really awesome experience I would say.

An humble Upma, tasted so nice, making me to say it was one of the best Upmas I must have eaten outside. Everything was so impeccable with its looks, texture, taste and it was doubly complimented by the Coconut Chutney served alongwith it.

Rasam Vada with Chutney was another great thing to savour, no complaints on it.

The Star of the show was Button Idly with Srilankan Curry -  something I am short of words to appreciate and explain. Sambhar replaced by Coconut based gravy in a bowl and button idlys immersed in them, so that they absorb all the flavours of the gravy within them, each bite of every piece of the Idly kept us craving for more! A very great and unique experience for us.

All this ended with a supurb dose of Filter Coffee, customised to our choice of regular or strong and that really left us super satisfied.

There is no parking available here, one has use the Pay and Parking place of the shopping mall just adjesannt to this place.

Overall, a must visit place if we happen to be in this area anytime. One may need to wait for tables, for its being occupied with people who are in no hurry while enjoying the food here!

featured_reviews.name: Prabinsum
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was a company audit done today by me and we posed as customers. Too many complains. Owners can take this as an advise in order to improvise.

1. Don't play music so loud that visitors find it difficult to talk. And if at all music is played don't connect your paytm payment notification tones and phone call rings on the same player. It's really annoying to hear your phone ringtones on speakers and also I'm not interested to know how much my next table person is paying.

2. Put curtains in the ac room. Ac cooling effect will be more and also too much harsh sun light coming inside. It's good if you have greenery outside. There you just have scorching sun. So better cover the glass.

3. When you have sugar packets on the table, then why waiter is asking wether we want with sugar or without sugar. It's improper customer service training. Train the waiters.

4. Make sure the menu has basic things. Being a south Indian Brahmin cafe if you don't have idli, it's not right. You have thatte idli but keep steamed idlis too.

5. Right after bill amount was received, the waiter immediately asked us - "aapka hogaya kya" he din't even wait for a second to ask this question which was unexpected and rude. Again lack of customer service skills. Respect your customers.

6. The staircase is too narrow and I understand. The interiors are nice. Place is well utilised. Hats off to that but when customers are already climbing down and waiter can see it, he should step down, he stood there like a pillar and we had to literally sqeeze and go through him and pass downwards. He should realise manners when there are female customers.

These small and simple things make huge difference. There may be customers who don't bother about all this but even 1% of dissatisfaction should not exist in any business.

Thank you !

featured_reviews.name: Hussain Shaherwala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Honestly, the best South Indian food that I have had till date. Truly authentic, very well made with lots of care.
The Sri Lankan curry with idli and Vada were just awesome, so is the sheera and all the dosas and idlis. But the main attraction and the showstopper was the benne dosa, which was crip from the outside and a bit soft from the inside, topped with amazing chutneys and their perfect sambhar. The filter coffee was also one of the best I have ever had.
The ambience is very attractive with cute cartoon decorations.
A must visit for true South Indian cuisine lovers.

featured_reviews.review_text: We recently visited South Indian Brahmin Cafe, and it was a delightful experience for any South Indian food lover. We sampled a variety of dosas—each perfectly crisp and flavorful. The thatte idlis were soft, fluffy, and generously served with lots of fresh, tasty chutneys and sambar. The sheera was comforting and just the right amount of sweet. We ended our meal with authentic filter coffee and refreshing fresh buttermilk, which rounded off the experience beautifully. Hygienic outlet. must visit for all Pure Veg and South Indian food fans!

featured_reviews.name: Vinay Pasi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Mutuswami Cafe in Khar and really enjoyed the overall experience. The place has a simple, casual vibe but serves a wide variety of dishes—from authentic South Indian options to Mumbai street-style favourites.

The benne dosa stood out with its crispy texture and buttery flavour, while the idli was soft and fresh. The cheese pav bhaji and mushroom sukha combo added a nice desi touch to the meal. The mango milkshake and mango sheera were rich, sweet, and perfect to end on a high note.

Service was quick, though it can get a bit crowded during peak hours. Overall, it’s a great place for breakfast or a casual meal with good food and decent pricing. Would definitely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: sourabh debnath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at muttuswami Khar🌟
Started with the refreshing Kala Khatta and Aam Panna coolers — both were perfect for the Mumbai heat. The Ghee Podi Idli was super soft and flavourful, while the Masala Benne Dosa was buttery, crisp and delicious. For mains, the Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam and Chettinad Biryani were packed with authentic flavours and tasted amazing. Ended the meal with Payasam and Vanilla Gelato which made for the perfect dessert combo. Great food, comforting flavours and an overall amazing dining experience. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Mahima Pal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited the Khar outlet recently and absolutely loved the whole experience 🫶🏻

The café has such a warm and cozy vibe with a perfect blend of authentic South Indian flavours and modern café aesthetics. Every dish felt comforting, flavourful, and beautifully prepared.

We started with the Cheese Onion Uttappa which was soft, perfectly cooked, and loaded with cheese without overpowering the authentic taste. The Mutuswami Special Benne Dosa with paneer was honestly one of the highlights 🤤 crispy on the outside, buttery, rich, and filled generously with flavourful paneer stuffing.

The Ghee Roast Mushroom with Appam was another standout dish. The appams were soft and fluffy while the mushroom preparation had a beautiful spicy South Indian flavour that paired so well together. We also tried the Paneer Cheese Grilled Sandwich which was super cheesy, crisp, and comforting.

For drinks, the Chikoo Milkshake was thick, creamy, and refreshing, while the Kala Khatta Cooler from their summer specials was tangy, nostalgic, and perfect for the Mumbai heat.
Ended the meal with Mango Sheera and it was the sweetest ending possible 🤌🏻 warm, rich, and full of mango flavour without being overly sweet.

Loved the quality, presentation, ambience, and overall experience. Definitely a place I’d love visiting again for comforting South Indian food with a modern twist.

featured_reviews.name: Komal Jaisingh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mutuswami is one of those simple, comforting south indian food places which serve superb food. Calm and relaxed vibe - no rush, no noise just pure happiness. We absolutely loved the Paper masala Dosa, and podi idli.. two of my favs here. Apart from that they also serve Grilled Sandwiches, Pav Bhaji and an amazing line up of dosas and juices.
Had to end our meal with the super amazing Pineapple Sheera and filter coffee !! Manawwar served us really well !

featured_reviews.name: harshad lagade
featured_reviews.review_text: South Indian place in Khar west, this place is open for 24*7. Authentic south indian vibes with good food. Apart from South Indian food, they also have  other food items like Pav bhaji and Biryani. We tried their special dosa, Iced Filter Coffee, Paneer Biryani and coffee Gelato. Overall we had awesome time. Do visit soon.

featured_reviews.name: FJT
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went to Muttuswami Café with my skeptical, firang partner. He loved it, and so did I.

We had the Muttuswamy Special Benne Dosa, which is a mix of Benne Dosa, Masala Dosa and Ghee Podi Dosa. We also had Idli Vada Rasam, Plain and Hazelnut Filter Coffee, and a Pineapple Sheera to top it off. All of it was delicious, as well as pleasing to the eye!

The restaurant has been done up beautifully - it feels like you're walking into another world. It's super clean, and all the little touches - from the dabbara set for the filter coffee, to the paan box for the mukhwaas - serve to further elevate the experience.

Special thanks to Gaurav for being so patient and helpful.

I only dock one star because the AC wasn't working, and it's upwards of 35 degrees C right now. But honestly, the food was worth it.

10/10, would recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Angel Trata
featured_reviews.review_text:
Loved that someone is doing the culture right. Beautiful restaurant with great interiors, the traditional wooden entry door, green plants on exterior, lovely high ceilings, beautiful ceiling detail, lovely wall art in subtle color tones, not loud and disturbing but understated elegance, the lighting and design were all impeccable
I loved the uniforms for wait staff, they all wore pristine white lungi and half sleeve shirts with a cloth on the shoulder
Very refreshing to see the traditional attire
All the staff was pleasant, warm, welcoming with big smiles
Food was delicious too, the ambiance really did it for me.
The price was extremely reasonable
They even have fresh churned ice creams.
We had the rasam, rasam Vada, aviyal and hoppers X 2  and tomato onion uttapa and the total was under 900INR

featured_reviews.name: Firdous Diaries
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pure South Indian comfort food with a beautiful ambience .
Crispy Sada & Masala Dosa, soft Malabar Parotta with rich Veg Kurma, flavorful Pav Bhaji, refreshing Mosambi & Pomegranate juices and a sweet Fruit Salad with Ice Cream .
Everything tasted fresh, authentic and perfectly balanced.
Beautiful , clean ambience with calm vibes, quick service and warm hospitality.Cafe Muttuswami, Khar West - a hidden gem for South Indian food lovers. Highly recommended & will definitely revisit.

featured_reviews.name: Al J
featured_reviews.review_text: Fantastic North Indian Feast at Copper Chimney, Juhu. We had an unforgettable dinner at Copper Chimney in Juhu – authentic, flavorful, and perfectly atomistic in every bite! The mixed grill was a star, juicy and smoky with an array of chutneys that added zesty punches of flavor. Paired with fluffy rumali rotis, buttery tandoori naan, and creamy paneer kurchan, it was pure indulgence. We sipped on refreshing Mumbai Mustani mocktails, and ended with the decadent Peshawari kulfi for dessert. The lively atmosphere was elevated by the attentive and friendly staff( Dave our server) , who made our evening seamless. Amazing food, drinks, and service all around – a must-visit for Mumbai foodies!

featured_reviews.name: Tina Wa
featured_reviews.review_text: Wow the food here is exceptional. I’m a female travelling solo for work and really enjoyed eating here. I had the veggie biryani and the dal. The portion was about 3x more than I could eat, and believe me, I tried! Amazing.

featured_reviews.name: Anish Karkera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Really sweet staff that will recommend what's best if you are confused with the extensive menu. I'm reviewing a while after I went so I have forgotten the names of the dishes but I'll try to keep it clear.
The gosht dum biryani was an absolute disappointment, for the price point the flavour was abysmal. It tasted just like lightly spiced rice with some meat. Not at all what to expect from a nice place like this.
The chicken tikka we had was lovely, super soft and delicious, paired perfectly with our beers.
The rumali roti and naan were also very good, soft and tasty. Cannot complain.
The main course I believe we had the murg rahra that we licked clean. Rich and tasty.
Definitely going back here again for the curries and kebabs. Skipping all rice items, total scam.

featured_reviews.name: Aditi Prabhu
featured_reviews.review_text:
I attended the currently ongoing  "Phulkari" event by Copper chimney a meticulously crafted, flavourful and colorful menu inspired by Phulkari. Phulkari, after all, is more than just an art; it symbolizes tradition, joy, and togetherness....the very spirit of Diwali.

Foods on the menu that are a must try-
✨ Rose rumali roti with a creamy and flavourful walnut malai dip- A crisp rumali roti with subtle hints of rose teams with a creamy mellow walnutty dip.
✨ Chukandar Tikki with Missi Roti: The absolute melt in the mouth " Chukandar Tikki" with Missi Roti made me think....Who knew beetroot could taste so good 😅
✨Tandoori Pineapple- Smoky, spiced and my personal favourite.(....yes, I am biased when it comes to spiced pineapple😅)

And if you have a sweet tooth....

✨ Mava gujiya: A classic and must have.
✨ Badam halwa with malai ice cream: Rich, creamy and  definitely not for the faint hearted 😅

Drinks:
✨ Phoolkari- A subtle and soothing drink inspired by Bagh phulkari
✨ Anar Da Bagh- Another beautifully crafted drink inspired by Bagh Phulkari

Overall, Phulkari by Copper Chimney feels like a cultural celebration on a plate through flavor, color, and creativity.

featured_reviews.name: Petra Nasr
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very nice atmosphere,  very nice food and Mukul was so helpful and nice with us and with my kid .. explaining any doubts for us and making sure that we're having a nice food experience
We'll sure come back
Highly recommended

featured_reviews.name: Himanshi Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently dined at Copper Chimney in Juhu and had a fantastic experience! The restaurant had a cozy ambiance with beautiful copper accents that added a touch of elegance to the place.
The food was absolutely delicious - each dish was bursting with flavor and cooked to perfection. I especially loved the butter chicken and garlic naan - they were simply mouthwatering. The service was top-notch as well, with the staff being attentive and friendly throughout the meal.
Overall, I highly recommend Copper Chimney in Juhu for anyone looking for a great dining experience. The combination of delicious food, inviting ambiance, and excellent service make it a must-visit spot in the area.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: RAHUL V
featured_reviews.review_text:
So i visited madras diaries which is located in bandra west i must say
The food,service,ambience 10/10
Restaurant have 2 types of seating area indoor and outdoor both. Ambiance is supper cozy cool and aesthetic.

The paratha was soo good with proper layerings of laccha and tried lemon rice

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Dethe
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a lovely experience at Madras Diaries. The food was authentic, flavorful, and reminded me of true South Indian taste. The ambience was cozy and the service was quick and friendly. Definitely a great spot for a satisfying meal!

featured_reviews.name: Narendra Bhuwalka
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries Bandra West now serves South Indian classics with a new chaat menu that is already a hit
You get tangy crunchy plates like pani puri and bhel along with crispy dosas idlis rasam shots and filter coffee
The drinks are refreshing and pair well with the bold flavorful and addictive chaat
The vibe is bright modern and cozy with warm colorful South Indian touches that feel like home
If you want variety great taste and an ambiance that lifts your mood this is the perfect comfort food fix with a chatpata twist

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Ashford
featured_reviews.review_text: I thoroughly enjoyed the Mysore Masala Dosa, Idli Vada, Mini Idli, Pineapple Sheera, and Filter Coffee. Every item was delightful. Food took a while to be served, but it was fine for us. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic South Indian comfort food in Juhu, Shiv Sagar does not disappoint. The Benne Dosa was perfectly crisp on the outside, soft inside, and generously coated with butter—exactly how it should be. Rich, flavourful, and absolutely satisfying.
The Thatte  Idli was equally impressive soft, fluffy, and light, served fresh and hot. Paired with their delicious coconut chutney and flavourful sambar, it made for a truly wholesome meal.
Service was quick, the place was clean, and the food quality was consistent. Definitely a reliable spot for South Indian food lovers. Will surely visit again! 😊

featured_reviews.name: Shiv

featured_reviews.name: Shaifa Hirji
featured_reviews.review_text:
The decor and overall aesthetic of this place are truly beautiful. The ambiance, design, and attention to detail make it feel like a high-end spot, and walking in, you definitely expect a premium dining experience. Unfortunately, while the space looks stunning, the actual experience did not live up to the expectations, especially considering the reputation and standard one would associate with a place like this.

The biggest issue by far was the number of bugs. There were so many insects flying around our table while we were eating, which completely ruined the experience. What made it even more uncomfortable was that the staff were actively killing bugs right next to us as we were dining, which felt extremely unhygienic and honestly quite disgusting. It completely took away from the enjoyment of the meal and made it hard to relax or even finish our food comfortably. For a restaurant of this level, this is simply unacceptable and needs serious attention.

In terms of the food, it was a mixed experience. The watermelon and pineapple juices were good — fresh, refreshing, and nicely prepared. The watermelon salad, however, lacked flavor and felt quite underwhelming, especially given how promising it sounded on the menu.

We ordered the edamame peas and the spicy chicken, and those dishes were actually quite good. They were well-cooked, flavorful, and enjoyable, which showed that the kitchen does have potential. However, good dishes alone cannot make up for poor hygiene standards and an uncomfortable dining environment.

The service also felt below expectation. It didn’t reflect the quality, attentiveness, or polish you would normally associate with a Bastian-level standard. Overall, the experience felt disorganized and lacking in the fine-dining attention to detail that one would expect.

In summary, while the decor is stunning and some of the food items were good, the bug issue and service quality seriously impacted the experience. It did not feel like a Bastian-standard restaurant, and until these issues are resolved, it’s hard to recommend. With better hygiene control, improved service, and more consistency in food quality, this place could truly live up to its potential — but for now, it unfortunately falls short.

1.This is the run and owned  by the same family who runs the matunga eatery since day one it opened in vile parle east i started frequenting this place  I must clearly point out my observations for this place
Food is not as perfected like the OG Arya bhavan at matunga i feel that  matunga  has good chefs and service staff to deliver Excellence this vile parle branch offers almost the same menu  but at  times I felt that the food goes haywire chutneys sometimes  are very  well prepared  but some times watery chutneys and half done dosas not done right.

2.i feel  owner should & MUST visit this place atleast 3 times a week though his son and the owner himself know me i feel the service and food here get wonky many  times as they have recently expanded to other branches in sewri chembur too hence staff issue remains a challenge in kitchen as well in service.

Idlis are well made nice fluffy perfected with their in-house spl batter u will notice the difference in the first bite itself

They have other variety of dosas like palak dosa Mysore dosa which go well select ur pick

Kanchipuram idli Brahman idli all are good

While ac works fine washroom is a challenge to use as water soap tissues hygeine are clear issues which owner has to address ASAP

this place  is way above the average south indian Udupi restaurants and its can be termed as a gem for south indian breakfast lovers it does decent "ghati" desi style pizza too few sandwiches freshly made juices and has started chaats

Showstopper is the goti sodas with flavours ,Ananda milk is stocked up and has handmade ice cream which  could definitely be tried chocolate Orange my personal favorite

Rassam wada is another gem in their menu but have it with pipping hot rasam  and freshly made vada

Their tomato Rasam served here is another favourite's I sometimes come here just to have that however matunga outlet  does it better

Filter coffee is decent served in traditional brass tumbler set with spl sugar

Parking is roadside avoid going on weekends public holidays

Must visit the place after 8.30am before noon on weekdays to avoid  any waiting reservation is not required they are there on swiggy zomato however eating food going there is recommended

Curd rice, bisse bille bhat pav bhaji all is served

Looking for variety seated service with ac  quality food  this is it!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re visiting Mumbai and searching for the best South Indian breakfast in Juhu, you cannot miss Benne Heritage Bangalore Dosa.

This place truly has a hype of its own — and after experiencing it firsthand, I can confidently say it deserves every bit of it.

As a North Indian, I had never even heard of a “Benne Dosa” before my trip. But the buzz around this spot was so strong among locals that I felt compelled to try it.

I arrived in the morning and ended up standing in line for nearly an hour just to get in — which might sound intense, but the experience began impressing me even before I entered. The staff personally came to people waiting in line, thanked us for our patience, and even offered sweets. That level of hospitality instantly set the tone and showed how much they value their customers.

Inside, the place is lively, energetic, and completely packed. This is not a traditional sit-down restaurant; most guests stand and eat, with designated tables only for elderly guests, pregnant women, small children, or those with medical conditions.

Ordering is fully digital through self-service screens — you select your items, pay, and receive a token. There’s also a glass-panel view of the kitchen so you can watch your food being freshly prepared, which adds to the authenticity and excitement. When your token appears, you collect your order downstairs and enjoy your meal.

On recommendation from regular customers there, I ordered the Benne Plain Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Donne Biryani, and Cold filter Coffee — and honestly, this turned out to be the most heavenly South Indian meal I’ve ever had anywhere, whether in India or abroad. The flavors were outstanding, the texture perfect, and every bite felt worth the wait. The iced filter coffee alone is reason enough to visit.

Another plus point: it’s surprisingly affordable. Most dosas range between ₹100–₹200, making it one of the best value-for-money food experiences in Mumbai.

They don’t deliver via Swiggy or Zomato, so you must visit in person — but trust me, that’s part of the charm. If you’re already going there, you might as well dine in and soak in the full experience.

Final verdict: If you love authentic South Indian food or are a food tourist exploring Mumbai, this place is an absolute must-visit.

Long queue or not, I would gladly wait again just to relive this meal. Without a doubt, this is my favorite South Indian food spot on earth so far.

Highly, highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text:
If comfort food had a personality, it would probably be Benne in Juhu. Benne - Heritage Bangalore Dosa has mastered the art of making South Indian food feel indulgent, nostalgic, and ridiculously satisfying all at once.

The star of the meal for me was easily the thatte idli - soft, fluffy, drenched in ghee, coated generously with podi masala, and honestly the kind of dish that instantly hits the spot. Every bite felt rich, comforting, and packed with flavour without trying too hard.

The dosas here deserve all the hype they’ve been getting across Mumbai food circles. I tried the Benne plain dosa, masala dosa, podi masala dosa, and garlic dosa - and somehow each one had a completely different personality. Crisp edges, buttery centres, perfect fermentation, and that signature Bangalore-style benne flavour that keeps lingering long after the meal ends. The chutneys deserve their own fanbase honestly - fresh, balanced, and addictive enough to want extra servings every single time.

The medu vadas were another standout - beautifully crisp on the outside, soft and airy inside, exactly how a good vada should be. And then came the filter coffee ice cream from their collab with Indu Ice Creams, which genuinely felt like the perfect ending to the meal. Creamy, strong coffee notes, slightly nostalgic, and an absolute must-try.

The space itself has a very minimal yet aesthetic South Indian café vibe - warm lighting, clean interiors, subtle Bangalore darshini-inspired energy, and an atmosphere that somehow feels both trendy and comforting together. A lot of diners online consistently rave about the crispy dosas, fresh chutneys, and ambience, and after visiting, it’s very easy to understand the obsession.

Overall, Benne feels less like just another dosa place and more like a love letter to Bangalore-style comfort food - buttery, soulful, and dangerously addictive.

Why is Nandu Dosas the best place in Mumbai to have dosas?

We all know that there are 100s of best places in Mumbai for dosas, but this one is beyond the best. It is simply so fine and tasty that even the best places seem dull in front of it. The place we are talking about is Nandu Dosa, located behind Ritumbara College, Vile Parle.

Sizzling Cheese Jinni Dosa
Nandu Dosa is famous for its Jinni Cheese Dosa, which is crispy in nature, stuffed with vegetables such as carrots, cabbage, and capsicum, adding spiciness and sweetness to the tangy, rich Schezwan sauce.
Bet it’s so tasty that you would order another one as you cannot resist its saucy nature and cheese-filled goodness.

Made with Fresh Batter
Nandu dosas are fresh in nature because the batter itself is made early in the morning, preserving its freshness for the whole day so that it doesn’t get spoiled.
If you try the idli as well, it still holds the freshness which feels like it was recently made — so yum, so tasty.

Its Famous Red Chutney
So sweet, so spicy — just tasting like a wow!
Yes, Nandu’s orange chutney is an absolute wow, made with cheese and chutney which has a sweet and spicy taste. Filled with red chili, tamarind, and roasted chana dal, it adds a perfect blend to the Jinni dosas.

Pro Tip
If you have an angry girlfriend and want to make her happy, take her to Nandu Dosas and order the Cheese Jinni Dosa.
See how her anger melts from anguish to just like the sweet orange chutney. This is one of the best ways to make her heart go from "hmm" to "uhmmm".

Nandu Dosas has a variety of dosas, but I would highly recommend trying the Jinni Dosa and Paneer Mysore Dosa, as these are the best-selling options and are always in high demand. They carry the authentic taste of South India while adding more variations to the South Indian culinary experience.

featured_reviews.name: Prabhjit Singh Modi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dosa and Thatte Idli both of them were good. What they could really add to the menu is some basic empathy.

I came from Vadodara after a 6-hour train journey and reached around 5:45 am. This was the first place I walked into straight from the railway station. At 6:00 am I politely asked the manager, the one with specs, if I could just sit in the corner since the space was empty and their setup was done. He flatly refused and said I could only enter at 7:00 am.

My back was hurting after the journey and I just needed a place to sit for a bit. It wouldn’t have cost them anything to show a little understanding. Instead, it was a straight no, no conversation.

If this were a smaller outlet, I’m pretty sure someone would’ve just said, “Haan bhai, sit.” Instead, he just didn’t allow it. No explanation, no actual rule, just a straight no. The place was empty, I wasn’t asking for free food, just a corner for 60 minutes after a 6-hour train ride. It honestly felt unnecessary and ego-driven.

That’s what happens when brands get big. A little success and suddenly basic decency becomes optional and Money gets to their head.

Massive respect though to the slim guy who seemed like the asst manager. He kept asking if I wanted to sit on his bike outside. That genuinely melted my heart. At least someone there understood basic humanity.

Food is good. The attitude needs serious work.

featured_reviews.review_text:
UPPU – A South Indian Kitchen in Bandra West is truly one of those rare places that gets everything right. I happened to visit UPPU in the last week of January 2026. From the moment you step in, the ambience immediately sets the tone. It’s warm, inviting, and thoughtfully designed — giving you a sense of comfort that makes you want to sit back and enjoy your meal without any rush. The interiors have a subtle South Indian touch, yet feel modern and elegant at the same time.

The food is where UPPU really shines. The taste is genuinely authentic — you can tell that attention has been paid to traditional recipes and flavours. Every dish feels carefully prepared, balanced, and true to its roots. The spices are not overpowering, the flavours are layered, and the overall experience feels wholesome rather than heavy. It’s the kind of place where you don’t just eat, you savour.

Another thing that stood out for me was the service. The staff is extremely well mannered, polite, and attentive. What I particularly appreciated is that they are present when needed but never intrusive. They don’t interrupt your dining or conversations unnecessarily, which makes the overall experience even more pleasant. It’s rare to find that perfect balance of attentiveness without interference.

Despite being located in Bandra West, where restaurants are plenty and competition is high, UPPU manages to create its own identity. It feels premium yet comfortable, refined yet relaxed. Whether you’re visiting for a family dinner, a quiet catch-up with friends, or even a business conversation, the setting works beautifully.

UPPU is a wonderful South Indian Restaurant and is definitely a place I would visit again and highly recommend to anyone looking for quality dining in Bandra West.

5/5 – An absolute gem that deserves far more recognition (Highly recommended)

Uppu serves exceptional South Indian fare, the dosas are perfectly crisp, the idlis are soft and fluffy, and every dish is prepared with care. The flavours are authentic and consistently excellent.

What sets this place apart is the warmth, the staff is genuinely courteous, the service is efficient, and the interiors are cozy without trying too hard. It’s the kind of neighbourhood spot that feels welcoming from the moment you walk in.

For those who queue endlessly at Benne, consider this your insider tip. Uppu is nearby, less crowded, and frankly, just as good, if not better. It’s close to home for me, which means I’ve been here enough times to know that this place deserves the footfall it hasn’t yet received.

"I recently visited shree sagar and was blown away by their dosa and idli! The dosa was perfectly crispy on the outside, yet soft inside, with a deliciously spiced potato filling that hit all the right notes. It came with a side of sambar and coconut chutney, which were both full of authentic flavors that complemented the dosa beautifully.

The idlis were light, fluffy, and melt-in-your-mouth soft, served warm with a generous helping of chutneys and sambar. I could tell that the batter was freshly fermented, giving them a subtle tanginess that’s hard to find.

Whether you're a fan of South Indian food or trying it for the first time, I highly recommend shree sagar Their dosa and idli are top-notch, and you’ll leave feeling satisfied and eager to come back!"

A consistently popular place that has witnessed (and outlasted) the rise and fall of the many so-called “trendy” restaurants lining 16th Rd.

Food: One of the best pav bhaji in Bandra, balanced flavours with depth. Ghee podi idli and bhindi fry were also tasty. Naan slightly more on the crunchy side, not a big deal.

Service: Busy but prompt.

Price: Affordable! 🤯 (considering it’s Bandra)

Atmosphere: Small but didn’t feel claustrophobic. It’s unfortunate that they have had to downsize, possibly due to the inflated rents and high competition in the area, but they seem to have managed it well. Music was subdued which made for easy conversation, a rarity among Bandra eateries these days.

featured_reviews.name: Nikhil Aher
featured_reviews.review_text:
Hidden Gem in Bandra — Better Than the Famous Benne Dosa Next Door!

Visited Shree Sagar Veg Restaurant (श्री सागर) in Bandra while waiting at the popular Benne Heritage Bangalore Dosa opposite, which had a 1.5-hour queue. Decided to try this place instead — and honestly, I’m glad I did!

The Benne Masala Dosa here was absolutely delicious — crisp, buttery, and perfectly balanced with their chutneys and sambar. It easily gives tough competition (and maybe even beats) the Benne Heritage one next door.

Simple, clean ambiance with quick service and authentic South Indian flavors. A must-visit if you love dosa and want a spot without the long waiting line.

featured_reviews.name: Food Chain Mumbai
featured_reviews.review_text:
Curry Patta, Near Bandra Talao, Bandra West.
I ordered food from this place yesterday and would to share my experience with you all.
Food items which I had are as follows:

•Chicken Chetinad: 5/5
Chicken Chetinad is a gravy made with boneless chicken pieces, turmeric, and coconut paste. This gravy was full of flavors and it was super delicious with paratha. In quantity wise I feel maximum 3 people can have it. Paratha was flaky, crispy and cooked well.

•Chicken Ghee Roast: 3/5
Soft juicy boneless chicken pieces roasted in ghee and in a sweet gravy.I had this with appam which is very much similar to a plain dosa but it also has coconut milk to it which makes it a bit on sweeter side.
Personally this dish was very sweet and sweetness should be reduced.

•Mangalorean Chicken: 4/5
Mangalorean chicken was so flavorful and tasty. It had all the delicious combinations right from the down South. Aroma & taste of coconut milk with spices to the gravy was such a delight to taste buds. I had this paratha and appam.

•Steamed Rice: 5/5
A small bowl full of plain cooked rice. Quality of the rice was good and it went really well with all the above dishes.

•Papd: 5/5
It was thin crispy and fried well.

I’d recommend people ordering food from here to have Chicken Chetinad, Mangalorean Chicken, Steamed Rice and Papad.
